Nina P: Quick Q 1: I booked an international flight for a conference. I used frequent flyer miles to upgrade the outbound to premium and paid the remaining cash taxes/fees on my personal card ($120). Can I expense the $120? Also do I need to declare the miles value anywhere?
Jordan (People Ops): Short answer: expense the cash taxes/fees, but we do not reimburse the monetary value of miles. Attach the itinerary and the card statement. Did you get manager nod for the upgrade?
Nina P: No manager pre-approval 1 1 1 it was a last-minute seat availability thing. Manager is OK with it after the fact.
Finance Bot: Policy excerpt: When employees use personal loyalty points/miles, company reimburses only actual out-of-pocket cash charges (taxes, carrier-imposed fees) if the travel itself was business-approved. Upgrades bought with cash require manager pre-approval; retro approvals accepted case-by-case. The notional value of miles is not reimbursed and is not reported as taxable income by Redwood.
Elena - Travel Admin: For the expense report: 1) Add one line "Airfare - carrier taxes/fees" $120, payment method: Personal Card. 2) Upload boarding pass/itinerary showing premium seat, and the loyalty transaction screenshot showing miles used. 3) Add a comment: "Manager retro-approval: Alex M".
Nina P: Uploaded itinerary, loyalty screenshot, card stmt. Added manager note. Anything else?
Finance Bot: Automated check passed. Total $120 within auto-approve limits. Will process as a standard reimbursement. No tax reporting required for miles usage per policy, but we keep documentation in the file.
Jordan (People Ops): Thanks for attaching everything. Note for future: if upgrade materially increases business benefit (e.g., longer overnight flight requiring rest), seek manager or People Ops pre-approval to avoid delays.
Nina P: Got it, thanks all :thumbsup:
